submission.natural_language_explanation: The pole fires on the sub-word token that carries the distinctive spelling of an uncommon, technical word - 'yl' in amyloid, 'oph' in Haemophilus, 'rob' in Agrobacterium, 'l' in angioplasty, 'ob' in trilobite, 'Cl' in Clostridium, 'micro' in microflora - and is about twice as strong when the sentence is about a technical subject (a bacterial list, a measurement of a substance) as when the same word is merely mentioned in a flat report frame. It stays near zero on technical vocabulary the model knows as frequent words (meningitis, cholesterol, Salmonella, Streptococcus, Escherichia, diabetes, bacteria) and on everyday nouns; its only common-word responses are extent/degree words used descriptively ('so severe', 'too little', 'a thin coat', 'far higher'), which reach 1.3-2.5 against the 2.2-3.6 technical peaks.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The county hospital's annual infection-control review began with a survey of the older wards, where the ventilation system had been installed decades earlier and had never been upgraded. Administrators noted that the wards still relied on shared bathrooms, a design choice that made hand hygiene difficult to enforce during busy shifts, and the nursing staff described the layout as a relic of a different era, when patients stayed for weeks and visitors came and went without badges. The committee spent the morning walking the corridors, checking sanitizer dispensers, and interviewing the housekeeping crew about their cleaning schedules. Several staff members mentioned that the dispensers were often empty by mid-afternoon, particularly on the surgical floor, where the turnover of beds was highest. The committee also examined the kitchen, where a walk-in refrigerator had been repaired twice in the same month, and the laundry, where the dryers ran continuously through the night. In the afternoon, the committee met with the laboratory director, who reported that a bronchial wash from a patient in the intensive care unit had grown Mycobacterium avium complex, a finding that prompted a review of the water system in that wing. The director explained that environmental cultures had been ordered from the shower heads and ice machines, and that the results would take several weeks to return. Members of the committee asked whether similar organisms had been recovered from other wards in previous years, and the director agreed to pull the archived records before the next meeting. The meeting ended with a short list of recommendations: replace the dispensers, install a dedicated line for the ice machines, and repeat the environmental sampling in the spring. The chair reminded everyone that the budget for the coming year would be tight, and that each request would need to be justified with data rather than anecdote. As the group dispersed, one of the nurses walked the chair to her car and mentioned, almost as an aside, that the night shift had been short-staffed for months and that the older wards had lost two senior nurses to a hospital across town. The chair made a note, closed her notebook, and drove home through streets that were still wet from the morning rain. She wondered whether the review would change anything at all, or whether the recommendations would be filed away with the ones from previous years.
